title: The Most Important Thing You Will Do In Your Life
author: Foundation Father
summary: This piece makes a blunt, values-driven argument that raising children well is the single most consequential thing most people will ever do, and that modern excuses for avoiding it — career ambition, travel, free time, a fear of being 'held back' — don't survive scrutiny once examined honestly. The author walks through how most people actually spend the free time they're protecting (TV, video games, phone scrolling) and argues that even genuinely meaningful uses of that time, like travel, gain their lasting value primarily from being shared with people you love, especially children. Rather than framing parenthood as self-sacrifice, the piece reverses the usual narrative: it cites data that fathers earn more than childless men and live longer, arguing children function as 'rocket fuel' for a man's life rather than a drag on it. The piece's persuasive strategy is less theological than practical and testimonial, closing with the author's own experience of his children rushing to greet him after a trip as evidence that the anticipated costs of fatherhood are consistently overestimated relative to its rewards.
points: Argues that most 'costs' people fear from having kids (lost travel, lost free time) are already being spent on low-value activities like TV, gaming, and phone scrolling.
Reframes children not as a constraint on a man's ambitions but as fuel for them, citing that fathers on average out-earn childless men by 3-10% and gain a longevity bump.
Contends that even meaningful experiences like travel only retain lasting value when shared with people you love, especially your own children.
Uses personal testimony (children rushing to the door after a trip) to argue people are systematically unprepared for how much joy parenting actually delivers.
quotes: For most people, the most important, consequential thing they will do with their lives is to have kids and raise them correctly. And yet, having children is the very thing that many people reject while at the same time complaining about meaningless lives.
You'll make some nice memories, make less of an impact than the ant you accidentally stepped on in Italy, and then eventually take those memories to your grave. No one else cares about them.
Having children and training up the next generation is the most important thing most people can do with their lives. There is no close second.
It's been well documented that, on average, men who are fathers make more than childless men, anywhere from 3% to 10%. Fathers also get a longevity bump and usually live longer.
Every time I come home from a trip, I walk in the door, set the luggage down, turn the corner, and my three kids are usually crammed together, trying to be the first to give me a hug.
